name: Phil Jackson
currentValue: The team that pays attention to this moment wins the most games.
correctedValue: The strength of the team is each individual member. The strength of each member is the team.
source: Eleven Rings: The Soul of Success (2013). This is his single most quoted line across Goodreads, QuoteFancy, and basketball coaching literature. It distills his Zen-meets-teamwork philosophy into one sentence. The current value ('pays attention to this moment') is a paraphrase that doesn't appear in any canonical quote database.
notes: Alternative candidates: 'The most we can hope for is to create the best possible conditions for success, then let go of the outcome.' But the team/member line is far more widely attributed and more recognisable as his signature.

name: Bessel van der Kolk
currentValue: 328 weeks on the NYT bestseller list. 3M+ copies.
correctedValue: Nearly 300 weeks on the NYT bestseller list. 3M+ copies sold in 36 languages.
source: Wikipedia (citing Literary Hub, Aug 2025) says 'nearly seven years' which is ~364 weeks, but the phrasing is approximate. Earlier Circana BookScan data (Apr 2024) reported 248 weeks and 3M+ copies. The book was still on the list through 2025. '328 weeks' is not sourced anywhere. The safest defensible claim is 'nearly 300 weeks' (the Wikipedia figure) or '250+ weeks' (BookScan 2024). Copies: 3M+ is confirmed by Circana BookScan.
notes: The exact week count is hard to pin because NYT doesn't publish cumulative totals. Wikipedia's 'nearly seven years' (~364 weeks) is the most recent figure (Aug 2025) but is approximate. The current value of '328 weeks' appears fabricated. Recommend using 'Nearly 300 weeks on the NYT bestseller list. 3M+ copies in 36 languages.' as a defensible middle ground. The copies figure of 3M+ is solid.

name: Eckhart Tolle
correctedValue: Oprah webinar series: 35M total views (not unique participants). A New Earth: 5M copies in North America. Power of Now: 16M copies worldwide.
source: HandWiki (Biography:Eckhart Tolle) and Wikipedia (A New Earth): 'By October 2009, the webinars had been accessed 35 million times.' The third webinar alone drew 11M+ viewers. The 35M figure represents cumulative accesses/replays across all 10 webinars, NOT 35M unique participants at one event. Power of Now: Wikipedia confirms 16M copies worldwide as of 2025.
notes: The current value is misleading. '35M participants' implies 35 million people sat in on a single webinar. The real figure is 35M cumulative accesses across the 10-week series including replays. Recommend: 'Oprah webinar series accessed 35M times. Power of Now: 16M copies worldwide.' This is accurate and still impressive.

name: Peter Levine
currentValue: Trauma is in the body, not the event.
correctedValue: Traumatic symptoms are not caused by the event itself. They stem from the frozen residue of energy that has not been resolved and discharged.
source: Waking the Tiger: Healing Trauma (1997), Section I: The Body as Healer. This is Levine's most cited formulation. The current value ('Trauma is in the body, not the event') is a reasonable paraphrase of his philosophy but is not a direct quote. His actual distillation is more specific about frozen energy in the nervous system.
notes: The current paraphrase captures the gist but loses the specificity that makes Levine's insight distinct from, say, Bessel van der Kolk. For a stupidSimplicity field that needs to be punchy, a shortened version like 'Trauma lives not in the event, but in the frozen energy your body never discharged' would be more accurate while staying concise. The full quote from the book is the one provided in correctedValue.

name: Peter Levine
correctedValue: VERIFIED. Peter Levine served as a stress consultant for NASA during the early development of the Space Shuttle.
source: Ergos Institute / SomaticExperiencing.com (official bio), GoodTherapy.org biography, Wikipedia (Peter Levine), European Association for Somatic Experiencing. All confirm: 'He served as a Stress consultant for NASA in the early space shuttle development.' This is consistently reported across his official bio, third-party bios, and Wikipedia.
notes: The NASA claim is well-sourced and appears on his official Somatic Experiencing website, Wikipedia, and multiple independent biographical sources. No reason to doubt it.

name: Marisa Peer
correctedValue: 10,000+ RTT therapists trained worldwide (per RTT School's own claim).
source: RTT Training Courses page (marisapeer.com) and rtt.com both cite 'a global community of over 10,000 RTT therapists.' This is a marketing claim from Marisa Peer's own organization. No independent verification of this number exists. Some third-party sources cite lower figures (6,000+). The number likely includes all graduates, not just actively practicing therapists.
notes: The 10,000+ figure is sourced only from Marisa Peer's own marketing materials. It cannot be independently verified. The distinction between 'trained' and 'certified' and 'actively practicing' matters. Recommend keeping the value but flagging it as a self-reported claim: '10,000+ trained through the RTT School (self-reported).' Confidence is below 90% because there is no independent verification.

name: Deepak Chopra
currentValue: You are not your body. You are the consciousness that observes it.
correctedValue: Every cell in your body is eavesdropping on your thoughts.
source: This is Chopra's single most widely quoted line across Goodreads, QuoteFancy, AZQuotes, and Addicted2Success. It distills his core mind-body philosophy into one memorable image. The current value ('You are not your body...') IS a real Chopra teaching (from Chopra Foundation), but it's more of a standard non-duality statement that could be attributed to many teachers. 'Every cell is eavesdropping' is distinctively Chopra.
notes: The current quote is genuinely Chopra's but reads as generic non-duality (could be Tolle, Mooji, etc.). The 'eavesdropping' quote is more distinctive, more memorable, and more widely attributed specifically to Chopra. It also connects better to his unique contribution: bridging consciousness with cellular biology.

name: Joe Dispenza
currentValue: Doctors said his broken spine needed surgery. He healed it with meditation.
correctedValue: Doctors said his 6 shattered vertebrae needed Harrington rod surgery. He refused and visualised his spine rebuilding for 10 weeks until he walked again.
source: Self-reported origin story told consistently across Lewis Howes podcast, Ed Mylett podcast, Greatness.com, and his own books/Instagram. In 1986, hit by a truck during a triathlon in Palm Springs. 6 vertebrae compressed/broken, 4 fracture sites, bone fragments near spinal cord. 4 surgeons recommended Harrington rod surgery. He refused, spent ~10.5 weeks doing mental reconstruction/visualisation, walked again at 10.5 weeks, back training at 12 weeks.
notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: This story is entirely self-reported. No independent medical records or third-party medical verification has ever been published. Dispenza is a chiropractor (DC), not an MD. Critics (Edzard Ernst, skeptic community) note there are no independently verified medical records. The story is consistent across his tellings but that only proves consistency, not truth. The current value is factually close but says 'meditation' when Dispenza specifically describes 'mental rehearsal/visualisation' not traditional meditation. Recommend keeping but noting it is self-reported.

name: Priya Parker
currentValue: The Art of Gathering shifted how an industry thinks about meetings and events.
correctedValue: National bestseller. Named Best Business Book of the Year by Amazon, Financial Times, and Bloomberg. TED talk viewed 3M+ times.
source: Penguin Random House, Amazon listing, TED.com speaker page, Mollie Plotkin Group (speaker agency). The book is confirmed as a national bestseller and won multiple Best Business Book awards. Her TED talk '3 steps to turn everyday get-togethers into transformative gatherings' has 3M+ views per her speaker agency bio. No specific copies-sold figure is publicly available.
notes: The current value is purely qualitative ('shifted how an industry thinks') with no verifiable metric. The corrected value provides concrete, verifiable metrics. Exact copy sales are not public. The TED talk view count of 3M+ comes from her speaker agency (Mollie Plotkin Group) rather than a direct YouTube count, but speaker agencies typically keep these current for booking purposes.
